title: Saturday, November 7
script:
Good morning. Today is Saturday, November seventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, we have partly sunny skies ahead today with a high near sixty-five degrees and calm winds out of the northeast. Rain chances sit at zero percent through both the day and night. Tonight turns partly cloudy as temperatures dip to a low around thirty-six degrees. The sun rose at six thirty-seven this morning and will set at five thirteen this evening.

Turning to the top headlines around the world. President Donald Trump has chosen Stephen Miller to take over as his chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. The staff shakeup follows sweeping Republican losses in Tuesday's midterm elections and sets up an aggressive posture heading into clashes with the new Democratic Congress. Trump confirmed on sixty minutes that personnel changes were imminent, hours before making the announcement. Down in South America, Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a sudden banking collapse left millions of citizens unable to access their savings. Pope Leo has begun a twelve-day, three-country tour of South America just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The trip takes him through Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, with the Vatican reporting the pontiff is in good health for his first journey to the region since the operation. In the United States, the incoming class of senators will include several historic firsts, featuring the first Native American woman elected to the chamber, the first Muslim senator, and the chamber's first Paralympian. Meanwhile, counting drags on in Mississippi's razor-thin Senate race between Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom, spotlighting the state's slow and decentralized counting process.

Moving to football, the Kansas City Chiefs return home to Arrowhead Stadium tomorrow to take on the two and six New York Jets. The Chiefs sit at five and two and are trying to snap a frustrating two-game losing streak. Last week, Kansas City controlled most of the game against Denver before a fourth-quarter collapse handed the Broncos a twenty-eight to twenty-four win. Head coach Andy Reid faces second-year Jets coach Aaron Glenn, with Kansas City entering as nine and a half point favorites. The injury report brings trouble on defense. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods is ruled out with a neck injury after missing practice all week, and rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane is also out. Off the field, wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy following numerous lawsuits tied to his twenty twenty-four car crash. For New York, running back Breece Hall is set to return to action, giving the Jets a much-needed boost after dropping three straight games.

On the college hardwood, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team rolled to a blowout victory over Middle Tennessee State at Allen Fieldhouse. Kansas entered the night favored by twenty-seven and a half points and put the game away early. Despite the lopsided win, head coach Bill Self noted postgame that he still has real concerns about his squad, pointing specifically to early-season struggles at the free-throw line. Roster adjustments are also in motion, with forward Trey Kaufman-Renn looking to earn a starting role after opening the year coming off the bench. The Jayhawks now turn their attention toward a heavyweight showdown against Kentucky.

Looking at fantasy football heading into Sunday's Week Nine slate, injuries are forcing tough lineup decisions. Running back Cam Skattebo is listed as doubtful, meaning fantasy managers must line up a replacement immediately. On the positive side, Travis Kelce is on track to play for Kansas City against the Jets, keeping him locked into starting tight end slots. For the Detroit Lions, wide receiver Amon-Ra Saint Brown remains on track to play against the Miami Dolphins. If you are weighing flex calls, Breece Hall's return pushes him ahead of Blake Corum, giving Hall clear lead-back volume despite facing Kansas City. In waiver news, running back Dameon Pierce is back on the market after being released by the Philadelphia Eagles with an injury settlement.

Heading out west to Los Angeles, summer-like heat continues for the weekend. Expect sunny skies today with an afternoon high reaching eighty-eight degrees and light north-northwest winds around five miles per hour. The rain chance is zero percent. Tonight stays mostly clear as temperatures drop to an overnight low of sixty-one degrees. Sunrise was at six eighteen this morning, and the sun will go down at four fifty-four this afternoon.

In entertainment news, casting for the next James Bond is heating up. Deadline and Variety report that Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult recently screen-tested for double-oh-seven with director Denis Villeneuve, joining fellow British actors Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor, and Callum Turner as contenders. On television, Netflix has officially ordered a Stranger Things spinoff titled Other Worlds, setting the new series in the nineteen-fifties. Meanwhile, Adam Driver confirmed he will not reprise his role as Adam Sackler in Lena Dunham's five-episode Girls revival, though he wished the production well. Across the sales market ahead of the American Film Market, Idris Elba is set to direct and star in the action-comedy In Laws, with filming scheduled for March in Spain. Rosamund Pike is attached to star in and produce Feed, an upcoming body horror film directed by Leslye Headland. And Korean drama The Remarried Empress set an all-time record for Disney Plus, scoring the streamer's biggest launch ever for a local original after debuting at number one across more than fifty global territories.

In tech and artificial intelligence, funding rounds are hitting historic figures. OpenAI is reportedly finalizing a fresh eleven billion dollar investment round that values the company at one point two five trillion dollars, even as rival Anthropic prepares for an upcoming initial public offering. Product rollouts also continue to pick up speed. Meta announced a new feature called Spaces for its Muse assistant, allowing users to build customized app-style interfaces, like dashboards and planners, using text prompts and connections to outside apps like Google Calendar and Notion. Amazon is rolling out an update letting shoppers text photos or descriptions directly to Alexa to place orders. Meanwhile, geopolitical tension around AI hardware is growing. The New York Times reports Chinese intelligence recruited an executive from Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang. Domestically, Tuesday's midterms showed rising community pushback, with voters approving restrictions on data center construction in forty out of forty-one local ballot measures nationwide.

Down in South America, Rio de Janeiro will see warm weather with a slight chance of rain today. Temperatures will climb to a daytime high near eighty-nine degrees with a nighttime low settling around seventy-two. There is a twenty-five percent chance of light showers, with wind gusts up to twenty miles per hour and a high UV index of nine. The sun rose at five oh four this morning and will set at six oh eight this evening local time.

Finally, turning to news across Brazil, the superior electoral court has officially launched an investigation involving President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin. In Rio de Janeiro, legal proceedings are moving forward in the death of American art dealer Brent Sikkema. A local Rio court scheduled a February twenty twenty-seven trial date for the Cuban national accused of carrying out the killing. Sikkema's ex-husband was recently sentenced to life in prison in federal court in New York for ordering the murder, while the accused hitman's defense claims an informal agreement with federal agents to avoid extradition. On the public safety front, the twenty twenty-six security yearbook ranked the coastal city of Macaé as the safest municipality in the state of Rio de Janeiro. And in sports, the father of superstar forward Neymar has officially taken over as chief executive officer of Brazilian top-flight club Santos.

That's the paper.

title: Friday, November 6
script:
Good morning. Today is Friday, November sixth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies today with a high near seventy-one degrees, though temperatures will drop to around sixty-six by the afternoon. Winds will stay light out of the north northeast at under five miles per hour, with only a one percent chance of rain. Tonight drops to a low around thirty-eight under mostly clear skies. There are no active weather alerts in the area. Sunrise is at six thirty-six a.m. and sunset is at five fourteen p.m.

Turning to national and world news, the fallout from the midterm elections continues to take center stage. Per The New York Times, Democrats have officially cleared two hundred fifty House seats, cementing a decisive shift in congressional power. At the same time, NPR reports that fears of an upcoming crackdown on artificial intelligence and data centers from the incoming Democratic majority sparked a massive two trillion dollar selloff in tech stocks, driving the Nasdaq down by more than five percent.

In Washington, a federal judge issued a midnight order blocking the construction of President Trump's proposed arch for fourteen days. As reported by the Washington Post, the ruling came just moments after a federal panel had approved immediate work on the structure.

Over in foreign affairs, NPR reports that First Lady Melania Trump helped broker a six-day pause in fighting in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky as the administration ramps up diplomatic efforts toward a lasting agreement. Meanwhile, Pope Leo the Fourteenth has begun a three-nation tour of Latin America starting in Uruguay, traveling just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.

Moving to football, the Kansas City Chiefs are preparing for their Sunday matchup against the New York Jets while reviewing their roster and performance. Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson was voted the Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week after racking up one hundred twenty-eight receiving yards in Week Eight, marking the highest single-game receiving yardage for an NFL running back this season. However, defensive tackle Peter Woods missed his second consecutive practice Thursday due to a neck injury. To add depth, Arrowhead Pride reports Kansas City signed wide receiver Bub Means and return specialist Jacob De Jesus to their practice squad.

Looking across the matchup, the New York Jets expect to get their star running back returned to action on Sunday in Kansas City. Meanwhile, league insiders have connected the Chiefs to Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs ahead of the trade deadline, as Kansas City searches for answers after losing momentum in close games against top opponents.

On the college court, Kansas men's basketball head coach Bill Self expressed serious concern over the Jayhawks' early free-throw shooting, warning that the team must clean up its execution at the line. Self also noted that he sees another level of potential for transfer forward Trey Kaufman-Renn and guard Melvin Council Jr. Kaufman-Renn told reporters he chose Kansas because he wants to be part of something special this season. Meanwhile, the Jayhawks men's team is coming off a recent win over Fordham, with players Leroy Blyden and Tre White reflecting on their performance as the squad continues its non-conference schedule. In former Jayhawk news, Kevin McCullar Jr. has secured a new NBA opportunity, signing a contract with the Toronto Raptors.

In fantasy football, crucial injury updates are changing weekly lineups. According to Yahoo Sports, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was upgraded to a limited participant in practice, offering positive momentum for his game-day availability. On the other hand, rookie running back Cam Skattebo remained sidelined on Thursday, making his status questionable and putting backfield backups into focus.

In Jacksonville, fantasy managers should track running back Bhayshul Tuten's injury status carefully, as backup option Sione Vaki could see an expanded role. Following Thursday night's battle between the Jaguars and Ravens, mid-week waiver wire activity is heating up, with wide receivers Tre' Harris and Brandin Cooks standing out as top high-upside bench stashes for Week Nine.

Out in Los Angeles, expect a bright and sunny day with a high near eighty-three degrees. Winds will stay gentle out of the north at around five miles per hour, with zero percent chance of rain throughout the day. Overnight, conditions will stay mostly clear with a low around sixty degrees. There are no active weather alerts for the region. Sunrise was at six seventeen a.m. local time, and sunset will be at four fifty-five p.m.

In entertainment news, Deadline reports that The New York Times Company is in advanced negotiations to acquire the film social network Letterboxd for a reported three hundred thirty million dollars, edging out rival bidder A24. At the box office, director Takashi Yamazaki's R-rated Godzilla Minus Zero opened strongly, pulling in approximately six million dollars in preview screenings.

In executive news, Helene Hahn Lloyd, a former Disney executive vice president and founding executive at DreamWorks, passed away at age seventy-eight. Meanwhile, Variety reports from the Taiwan Creative Content Fest that Weta FX chief executive Daniel Seah warned major Hollywood studios have completely shifted their stance on generative artificial intelligence, noting that major studios now demand that visual effects vendors present a clear AI strategy.

In technology news, OpenAI introduced GPT-six Cyber, a specialized model designed to identify software vulnerabilities and assist with security testing. OpenAI stated that the model uncovered eighty-one security flaws in Firefox while demonstrating improved safety guardrails during testing. The company also announced it will stop utilizing non-disclosure agreements with public officials regarding data center developments following election backlash over infrastructure projects.

In other tech updates, TechCrunch reports that Anthropic launched a Personal Finance feature within Claude, allowing users to connect their bank accounts through Plaid to evaluate spending patterns. Perplexity announced a new capability called Teammates, providing always-on AI agents that can work collaboratively across complex ongoing tasks. Additionally, Palo Alto Networks is in negotiations to purchase AI security startup Clutch for five hundred million dollars.

Down in South America, Rio de Janeiro will experience light drizzle today, reaching a high near eighty-one degrees Fahrenheit and dropping to a low of seventy-four. The area faces a twenty-nine percent chance of precipitation, with wind gusts reaching up to twenty miles per hour. Sunrise was at five zero four a.m. local time, and sunset will take place at six zero eight p.m.

In national news from Brazil, Interscope Records announced its expansion into the Brazilian market through a new joint venture with hip-hop artist BK and Supernova Entertainment. On the energy front, domestic ethanol output is projected to reach a record forty-six point three billion liters in twenty twenty-seven, triggering concerns among producers over falling profit margins due to an impending supply glut.

In local news from Rio de Janeiro, a United States court sentenced the ex-husband of an American gallery owner murdered in Rio's Jardim Botânico district to life in prison. Local prosecutors have also requested the arrest of a military police officer suspected of killing a university professor along the Dutra highway. Meanwhile, Rio law enforcement deployed three hundred sixty officers in Realengo targeting stolen vehicle rings, while a separate operation in Botafogo seized weapons and recovered stolen municipal sanitation containers.

That's the paper.

title: Thursday, November 5
script:
Good morning. Today is Thursday, November fifth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, expect patchy morning fog before nine a.m., giving way to a sunny day with a high near seventy-five. Temperatures will fall back toward seventy in the afternoon with light winds. Tonight will be mostly clear with a low around forty-six degrees. There are no active weather alerts, and rain chances remain under two percent. Sunrise was at six thirty-five a.m. and sunset will be at five fifteen p.m.

Turning to national and world news, NPR reports that a federal panel is meeting Thursday to consider final approval for President Trump's proposed arch, with the government indicating construction could begin later in the day despite critics hoping a judge will block it. Meanwhile, the political aftermath of Tuesday's midterm elections continues as Democrats take control of Congress. BBC reports Vice President Vance offered a scathing election critique blaming the war in Iran, while analysts note that lower gas prices are unlikely soon due to global oil market complexities. Overseas, prominent Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to ten years in prison under Beijing's national security law. In sports legend news, BBC reports Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international duty for Portugal. Finally, Pope Leo hosted singer-songwriter Bob Dylan for a brief meeting at the Vatican.

In football, the Kansas City Chiefs are picking up the pieces following a twenty-eight to twenty-four loss to the Denver Broncos that dropped them to five and two on the season. Arrowhead Pride reports that despite the loss, rookie running back Emmett Johnson shined with five catches for one hundred twenty-eight yards, including a seventy-three yard touchdown. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that Harrison Butker will remain the team's starting kicker for Week nine against the New York Jets, leaving veteran practice squad signee Justin Tucker on reserve for now. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods missed practice after suffering a neck injury early in Sunday's game. Looking ahead to Sunday's opponent, KCTV reports that Jets star wide receiver Garrett Wilson has entered concussion protocol ahead of their matchup with Kansas City.

Moving to college basketball, the Kansas Jayhawks men's team is gearing up for their next game against Middle Tennessee State. Yahoo Sports reports that head coach Bill Self is managing a deep roster this year, creating intense competition for playing time across the lineup. Freshman Akira Jacobs has already caught attention with his calm play on the floor as the team looks to build early momentum.

On the fantasy football front, wide receiver waiver wire pickups are highlighted by veteran Keenan Allen, while target trends show rising value for Adonai Mitchell. Heavy injury news dominates the mid-week reports, per NBC Sports. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is likely out for the remainder of the season, and running back Jeremiyah Love has been placed on injured reserve. Elsewhere, New York Giants rookie Cam Skattebo was sidelined from Wednesday's practice, and wide receiver Denzel Boston was limited with a calf injury.

Out in Los Angeles, you can expect a mostly sunny Thursday with a high near eighty degrees and light north winds. Clear skies will continue into Thursday night with a low dropping to around fifty-eight degrees. Rain chances are zero percent with no weather alerts in place. Sunrise was at six sixteen a.m. and sunset will be at four fifty-six p.m.

In entertainment news, Deadline reports that Channel Four has officially canceled Married At First Sight U.K. following external reviews into contestant welfare and recent rape allegations surrounding the show. On the film side, Sony Pictures Entertainment reported a record second-quarter profit of five hundred eighty-one million dollars, representing a five hundred twenty-seven percent surge driven largely by the massive box office performance of Spider-Man: Brand New Day. In script development, DC Studios has tapped Francis Galluppi to write a new John Constantine feature film, fresh off his work on Evil Dead Wrath. Additionally, former longtime Los Angeles television news anchor Harold Greene has passed away at the age of eighty-two.

In technology, OpenAI announced that ChatGPT can now generate animated GIFs natively from prompts or uploaded photos using its new Images two point six model, allowing users to edit frames and playback speeds. Meanwhile, TechCrunch reports that startup Nothing is launching its first screen-free AI device next month, described by CEO Carl Pei as a productivity tool built with personality. On the corporate side, Apple is reportedly cutting its internal AI budgets for engineering teams, while Uber revealed during an earnings call that only four rides were booked using third-party AI agents during the entire third quarter. Furthermore, midterm election results showed strong public pushback against AI data centers, with seventy-six percent of polled voters opposing local data center expansion.

Heading south to Brazil, Rio de Janeiro is looking at a warm and wet Thursday with light showers and a high near ninety-one degrees. Rain chances sit at seventy-five percent, with potential wind gusts reaching up to fifty-three miles per hour and a high UV index of nine. Tonight's low will settle around seventy-four degrees. Local sunrise was at five oh five a.m. and sunset will be at six oh seven p.m.

In Brazilian news, Dataconomy reports that a Brazilian court has barred Meta from using local media content to train its artificial intelligence models, siding with news publishers. On the sports pitch, Sky Sports reports that an under-twenty soccer match between Uberlandia and Mamore set a world record after the referee issued fifty-three red cards following a massive brawl. Locally in Rio de Janeiro, Radio Manchete reports that Federal Revenue officers seized fifteen tons of irregular goods at the Port of Rio. The city also experienced a wild weather night, with over three thousand lightning strikes recorded across the metropolitan area during the early morning hours, while local news reports a school wall collapsed in the Tijuca neighborhood.

That's the paper.

title: Tuesday, November 3
script:
Good morning. Today is Tuesday, November third, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, you are looking at a wet and stormy day ahead. Expect showers and thunderstorms before five p.m., with a high near seventy-two degrees, though temperatures will fall to around sixty-eight in the afternoon. Winds will come from the south southwest at five to ten miles per hour, with gusts reaching up to twenty-five miles per hour. Total rainfall could reach between one and two inches, with a ninety-three percent chance of precipitation. Tonight, skies will clear up nicely, bringing a much cooler low around forty-six degrees and light winds from the west. Sunrise this morning is at six thirty-four a.m., and sunset will arrive at five seventeen p.m.

Turning to the major news headlines, today is Election Day across the United States, with control of Congress hanging in the balance and results set to start rolling in as polls close. In international developments, the United States military carried out limited and defensive airstrikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, an action described by officials as defensive ahead of the midterms. In Ukraine, a devastating Russian bombing at an aid center in the south killed twenty-nine people, drawing sharp condemnation from Kyiv. Meanwhile, the United States Supreme Court rejected a last-minute push by the Department of Justice and the Trump administration to separate or discard disputed ballots in California. In cybersecurity news, NPR investigations revealed that hackers are increasingly targeting industrial refrigerators worldwide, exposing critical vulnerabilities in operational technology. Additionally, researchers report a rising wave of anti-Indian hate in the United States, highlighting risks faced by South Asian communities.

Moving to football and the National Football League, we start with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Chiefs are licking their wounds following a twenty-eight to twenty-four collapse against the Denver Broncos, a devastating loss that saw Kansas City blow an eleven-point fourth-quarter lead and drop to five and two. Head coach Andy Reid addressed the media on Monday, pointing to self-inflicted mistakes and stalled drives as the primary reasons for the blown lead. Meanwhile, general manager Brett Veach is actively scouting the wide receiver market ahead of the trade deadline, especially with Tyquan Thornton out for the season. Looking ahead, the Chiefs are preparing for their upcoming matchup against the Jets. Across the rest of the league, the AFC playoff picture finds the Buffalo Bills, Denver Broncos, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Jacksonville Jaguars leading their respective divisions as the midseason race heats up.

Sticking with basketball and the Kansas Jayhawks, the men's team opened their regular season in dominant fashion, cruising to a thirty-point victory over Fordham at Allen Fieldhouse. In recruiting news, five-star small forward Malachi Jordan has narrowed his final list down to three schools, with the Jayhawks remaining firmly in the mix alongside Saint John's and Vanderbilt.

For fantasy football managers navigating the week nine waiver wire, rookies like Mike Washington and Antonio Williams are trending upward as strong additions, alongside wide receiver Brian Thomas Junior who leads recent target charts. If you are setting your lineups, keep a close eye on the injury report, where players like Jakobi Meyers are managing lingering hamstring and ankle issues.

Checking the weather in Los Angeles, you will experience a pleasant and clear day. Expect mostly sunny skies with a high near seventy-five degrees and light winds out of the west northwest at zero to ten miles per hour. Tonight will stay mostly clear and comfortable, with a low around fifty-five degrees and northwest winds ranging from five to ten miles per hour. There is zero chance of rain today. Sunrise is at six fourteen a.m., and sunset will occur at four fifty-seven p.m.

In Hollywood and entertainment news, Simon Stone's film Elsinore has dominated the British Independent Film Awards nominations, pulling in twelve nods including a best lead performance recognition for Andrew Scott. Meanwhile, The Walt Disney Company is preparing for another wave of layoffs targeting up to twenty percent in cost savings across multiple divisions, including television networks and motion picture studios. On the streaming and international front, the highly anticipated Korean romantic drama series The Remarried Empress surprised fans by releasing its first four episodes a day early on both Disney Plus and Hulu.

Over in tech and artificial intelligence, Anthropic has updated the system prompt for its Claude Code tool to prevent users from generating direct video game clones, though building original games remains fully supported. Meanwhile, OpenAI announced its new Grid Protectors Program, planning to pilot data center power plants that can release up to one thousand megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies to support nearby local grids and homes. In legal news, The York Times and several other publications have filed lawsuits against the privacy-focused web browser Brave, alleging unlawful web scraping to train artificial intelligence models and bypass publisher paywalls.

The weather in Rio de Janeiro calls for heavy drizzle throughout the day. Expect a high near eighty-six degrees Fahrenheit and a low around seventy-three degrees. There is a seventy-six percent chance of rain, with wind gusts reaching up to twenty-six miles per hour and a high ultraviolet index of nine. Sunrise in Rio is at five oh six a.m., and sunset will take place at six oh six p.m. local time.

In Brazilian news, state water utility Cedae is carrying out its annual maintenance on the Guandu System today. Locally in Rio de Janeiro, city hall has guaranteed free bus transportation for students participating in the upcoming national exams. Across the wider country, the state civil defense reports that forty-seven out of sixty-two municipalities in Amazonas are in a state of emergency due to severe drought conditions impacting nearly one hundred forty-six thousand families. Additionally, the credit bureau Serasa announced that a record eighty-four million Brazilians carried overdue debts in September, with average debts hitting about one thousand three hundred five dollars per person.

That's the paper.

title: Monday, November 2
script:
Good morning. Today is Monday, November second, twenty twenty-six. Five oh five a.m.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, expect patchy fog before ten a.m. and a slight chance of rain showers around noon, with mostly cloudy skies and a high near seventy-eight degrees. South-southeast winds will move at zero to ten miles per hour, with gusts up to twenty-five miles per hour. Tonight, rain showers are likely starting around midnight, turning into showers and thunderstorms, with a low around sixty-one, and temperatures rising to sixty-five overnight. Active weather alerts are none. Sunrise is at six thirty-three a.m. and sunset will be at five seventeen p.m.

In top headlines, a small business jet nosedived into a South Florida neighborhood near President Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort, killing all nine people on board. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash a horrific tragedy, and officials confirmed the flight had departed Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. Meanwhile, Qatar is leading intense mediation efforts to prevent a new round of U.S. attacks on Iran following Tuesday's midterm elections, leaving the entire Gulf region on edge. In the cryptocurrency sector, Binance users withdrew three point six billion dollars after the exchange suffered its largest-ever hack, an incident linked to a North Korean group. Also, the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the disputed territory of Western Sahara officially ceased operations on Sunday after thirty-five years, following claims from both Morocco and the Polisario Front. In national news, college admissions offices are trying to become friendlier and less intimidating as student numbers remain scarce, while Senator Chris Murphy is expected to fully recover after being hospitalized following a stroke.

Moving to football, the Kansas City Chiefs saw their winning momentum stall in a twenty-eight to twenty-four loss to the Denver Broncos, falling to five and two and surrendering the AFC West lead. Patrick Mahomes finished thirty-one of forty-two for three hundred twenty-seven yards and three touchdowns, but the Chiefs blew a twenty-four to thirteen fourth-quarter lead after a missed fifty-four-yard field goal, a fifty-one-yard connection from Bo Nix to Jonah Coleman for the go-ahead score, and a final possession that reached the Denver one-yard line before a false start and a sack ended the comeback. During the game, rookie defensive lineman Peter Woods suffered a neck injury and was ruled out, while offensive lineman Kingsley Suamataia was benched for the second time this season in favor of Mike Caliendo. The Chiefs return home to Arrowhead Stadium in Week Nine to host the two and six New York Jets as nine and a half point favorites. Around the league, the loss dropped Kansas City behind the now six-and-two Broncos in the division standings.

In Kansas basketball, the season is officially underway as the Jayhawks and Tyran Stokes host the Fordham Rams at Allen Fieldhouse.

For fantasy football, the Week Nine waiver wire brings targets like Adonai Mitchell, Mike Washington Junior, Emmett Johnson, and Gardner Minshew. Several injury updates loom large across the NFL, including Lions linebacker Jack Campbell staying overnight at the hospital after a scary injury, Bears wide receiver DJ Moore avoiding major concern after a late-game scare, and Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love getting hurt against the Cowboys.

Looking at the weather in Los Angeles, today will be mostly sunny with a high near seventy-five degrees and west-southwest winds around five miles per hour. Tonight brings partly cloudy skies and a low around fifty-seven with north winds up to five miles per hour. Active weather alerts are none. Sunrise is at six thirteen a.m. and sunset will be at four fifty-eight p.m.

In Hollywood, Jesse Eisenberg’s comedy The Debut, starring Julianne Moore as a shy housewife who discovers a passion for amateur theater, will open the twenty-third Marrakech International Film Festival later this month. Netflix is undergoing layoffs in its London office, cutting roughly two to three percent of its staff, which includes senior figures like VP of Production Anna Mallett. Meanwhile, Goodfellas has unveiled the first images for Toho’s sci-fi thriller Leviathan, a live-action adaptation of Shiro Kuroi’s best-selling manga set in twenty-one twenty-seven, ahead of the American Film Market. Simon Pegg, Mark Duplass, and Haley Joel Osment are also teaming up for the dark comedy My Phone Died, which Hyde Park is taking to sales.

In tech and AI, OpenAI is reportedly exploring a rebrand of its data centers, considering the term AI compute campuses to help soften public perception. In hardware and industry, ZKH and Intel have teamed up to launch LingLong Insight one point zero, an edge AI model designed to verify industrial supplies and flag part mismatches before workers confirm delivery. Meanwhile, Spotify is reportedly weighing an AI remix add-on that could cost an extra four to five dollars a month, and Alibaba Group has partnered with Apple to integrate the Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence.

Checking the weather in Rio de Janeiro, today brings thunderstorms with hail, a high near eighty-five degrees, and a low around seventy-two. There is a sixty-nine percent chance of rain, with wind gusts reaching twenty-eight miles per hour and a UV index of nine. Sunrise is at five oh seven a.m. and sunset is at six oh five p.m. local time.

In Brazil and local Rio news, a broken pipeline in the Irajá community in Rio's North Zone flooded twelve homes and caused major destruction. In other news, the Rio de Janeiro municipal government announced it will offer free public transportation for candidates taking the upcoming national high school exam, known as the Enem, starting Sunday. On the economic front, Brazil's ICT sector attracted a record five point six billion dollars in foreign direct investment so far this year, while energy firm EDP secured a transmission project worth fifty-eight million dollars in a recent federal auction. Additionally, Brazil's race to orbit is ramping up with 3D printing training as BIZU Space joins EOS, and a Rio court is investigating a student group over allegations of racism directed at Marielle Franco.

That's the paper.

title: Sunday, November 1
script:
Good morning, it is Sunday, November first, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with the local forecast here in Arkadelphia, you can expect patchy fog clearing out before seven a.m., giving way to partly sunny skies with an afternoon high near seventy-eight degrees. Winds will stay quiet out of the northeast, and rain chances remain low at just six percent. For tonight, skies turn mostly cloudy with an overnight low dropping to around fifty-eight degrees and winds remaining light. There are no active weather alerts in the area. Sunrise was at six thirty-two a.m., and sunset is scheduled for five eighteen p.m.

Moving into the top national and world headlines, a federal judge has dismissed Donald Trump's ten billion dollar defamation lawsuit against Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal. The lawsuit stemmed from reporting on a nineteen ninety-three birthday letter allegedly sent by Trump to Jeffrey Epstein. In the ruling, United States District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the case with prejudice, stating the president failed to prove actual malice and calling the legal claims an exercise in grasping at straws. Meanwhile, another federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to cease issuing threatening letters to state election officials after communications demanded they set aside ballots of potential non-citizen voters ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections.

Overseas, massive street demonstrations over the rising cost of living and strained public services swept through European cities over the weekend. In France, the interior ministry reported that over three hundred twenty thousand people took to the streets nationwide on Halloween, leading to sporadic clashes with police. In Germany, coordinated cost of living rallies across Berlin, Hamburg, and Frankfurt turned chaotic, resulting in property damage and widespread shop looting.

On the financial and cybersecurity front, the Federal Bureau of Investigation confirmed that North Korea was behind a staggering six point three billion dollar cryptocurrency hack targeting Binance. The exchange announced that it will cover ninety percent of the customer losses resulting from the breach. In Washington, the Supreme Court heard oral arguments in a high-profile religious liberty case involving the Archdiocese of Denver, which is seeking legal permission to exclude LGBTQ families from enrolling in state-funded Catholic preschool programs.

Turning to the gridiron, the Kansas City Chiefs travel to Denver this afternoon for an important AFC West rematch against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Kickoff is scheduled for three twenty-five Arrowhead time on CBS. The five and one Chiefs previously handled Denver thirty-one to ten in the season opener, but the five and two Broncos have won five of their last six games since, including a thirty to sixteen win over Arizona. Kansas City is looking to rebound after dropping their first game of the season to Seattle, where third-down defense proved costly after allowing eleven conversions on sixteen attempts. On the injury front, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane was downgraded to out due to a lingering shoulder issue, and veteran defensive back L'Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve. For Jayhawks basketball fans, there is no major news for the Kansas men's basketball program this morning as the team wraps up its final preseason preparations.

Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have officially been ruled out for Week Eight action, while Chicago wideout DJ Moore and Buffalo tight end Dalton Kincaid remain game-time decisions with questionable designations. Out on the West Coast, rain is rolling through Southern California today. Los Angeles will see cloudy conditions with rain likely before four p.m., accompanied by a sixty percent chance of precipitation and a daytime high reaching near sixty-nine degrees. Rainfall totals should stay under a tenth of an inch during the day following heavier morning showers. Skies will clear up significantly tonight, leaving mostly clear conditions with a low falling to fifty-five degrees and north winds between five and ten miles per hour. There are currently no active weather alerts. The sun rose in Los Angeles at six twelve a.m., and sunset will arrive at four fifty-nine p.m.

In entertainment news, Saturday Night Live leaned heavily into Halloween and recent headlines for its latest broadcast. Host Inde Navarrette made her Studio Eight H hosting debut, taking a comedic swipe at Shane Gillis while discussing her physical training routine to play Rogue in the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe reboot of X-Men. The cold open featured Tom Hanks reprising his David S. Pumpkins character alongside James Austin Johnson's Donald Trump and Saidah Belo-Osagie portraying Nicki Minaj. Later in the episode, the newly crowned World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers brought their trophy to Weekend Update, joining returning alumnus Bobby Moynihan in character as Drunk Uncle. The show also paid tribute to the late Patrick Stewart, airing an archival clip from his nineteen ninety-four hosting appearance following his death at age eighty-six. In film updates, director Taika Waititi pushed back against negative critical reviews of his adaptation of Klara and the Sun, labeling dismissive reviewers as sad lost souls who are out of touch. Meanwhile, director Takashi Yamazaki and stars Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe received a standing ovation at the Tokyo International Film Festival for two sold-out screenings of Godzilla Minus Zero ahead of its Japanese theater release this Tuesday.

In tech, OpenAI has reportedly trimmed down the funding target for its latest capital raise as venture expectations face greater market scrutiny. Apple executives addressed the broader industry landscape this weekend, stating that the company has no interest in shipping artificial intelligence merely for the sake of shipping features. At the same time, regional reports confirm Apple is integrating Alibaba's Qwen model to support its Apple Intelligence software for iOS devices sold in mainland China. Over at Google, the company is testing an experimental artificial intelligence data center housed inside an orbital satellite, alongside the unveiling of Gemini Four Carbon, a specialized model tailored to autonomously locate and repair computer software vulnerabilities. In the courtroom, a federal judge has ruled that an NAACP lawsuit against xAI may proceed, with the organization alleging that the company's data facilities violate standards set by the federal Clean Air Act.

Looking at the international forecast down in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, the city is in for an overcast Sunday. Temperatures will peak near seventy-nine degrees Fahrenheit before dipping to an evening low around seventy. The chance of rain stands at ten percent, though coastal winds could produce gusts of up to thirty miles per hour, and the local ultraviolet index sits at a high rating of nine. Sunrise in Rio took place at five oh seven a.m. local time, and sunset is expected at six oh five p.m.

Closing out with developments in Brazil, state-controlled oil company Petrobras reached a landmark market valuation of one hundred forty-eight billion dollars, marking an all-time high for the energy producer. On the diplomatic calendar, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva confirmed he will travel to Turkey to participate in the upcoming COP thirty-one international climate summit. Back home, federal authorities have filed a formal lawsuit reviewing financial payments connected to Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, and the federal government announced increased protective security around indigenous Guarani-Kaiowa communities following recent security threats. Additionally, national employment regulators reported a seventy-five percent spike in formal complaints concerning workplace coercion and employer pressure during the election season. In local Rio de Janeiro news, municipal public health data reveals a significant spike in mpox cases, with current case counts now exceeding the total recorded across the entirety of last year. On a more positive note for city health services, Rio officials formally concluded a major meningitis immunization campaign after successfully administering four hundred fifty thousand vaccine doses across the metropolitan area.

That's the paper.

title: Saturday, October 31
script:
Good morning. Today is Saturday, October 31, 2026. Local time is five forty-one a.m.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, today brings cloudy skies with a high near seventy-one degrees and an east southeast wind at zero miles per hour. There is a forty percent chance of rain showers after ten in the morning, with new rainfall amounts expected to stay under a tenth of an inch. Tonight brings a fifty percent chance of showers and thunderstorms before lowering slightly later, with a low around fifty-five degrees that will rise to around fifty-nine overnight. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise will be at seven thirty-one a.m., and sunset at six nineteen p.m.

Turning to top headlines around the world, oil companies are reporting another quarter of sky-high profits, per NPR, as the ongoing war in Iran pushes up the price of oil and drives up costs at the pump. BBC News reports that the United States has approved the sale of five hundred Patriot missiles to Ukraine, providing American-made interceptors that remain crucial for downing Russian ballistic missiles. In the front-line town of Oleshky, BBC News notes that hundreds of people have been evacuated from the Russian-occupied area during a rare ceasefire, though many residents chose to stay despite the dangers. NPR also reports that a federal judge is opening a formal inquiry into potential Department of Justice misconduct in the Trump golf course case, investigating whether officials misled the court about their plans for the East Potomac municipal golf facility. In economic developments, a century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec, has indefinitely closed after the US imposed fifty percent tariffs on its products, putting hundreds of local residents out of work per BBC News.

In professional football, the Kansas City Chiefs hit the road to take on the Denver Broncos this Sunday afternoon in a high-stakes AFC West matchup. The Chiefs enter the game at five and one overall, looking to bounce back following a tough team-wide loss to the Seattle Seahawks last week. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that cornerback Mansoor Delane is listed as questionable for Sunday after suddenly missing practice on Thursday and Friday with a recurring shoulder injury that has lingered since training camp. In roster moves reported by NFL.com, the Chiefs have signed veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad. Across the league, the Denver Broncos prepare to host the rematch holding a five and two record, while analysts and former players continue to weigh in on Patrick Mahomes and the team's offensive adjustments ahead of kickoff.

Turning to Kansas men's basketball, the team is entering the final stretch of preseason preparations following its recent exhibition games. Preseason power rankings have dropped to highlight the top Jayhawks players heading into the campaign, while deep dives into the roster's depth continue under Bill Self.

For fantasy football managers sorting through lineups in Week 8, injury reports require close attention as players like Breece Hall and A.J. Brown navigate final game-day designations, while owners hunt for quarterback and tight end streamers. The waiver wire features key bench stashes and short-term fixes as the fantasy season reaches its midpoint.

Shifting to the weather in Los Angeles, today brings steady rain and cloudy skies with a high near sixty-eight degrees and a south southwest wind around five miles per hour. Rain will continue through the night with a low around fifty-nine degrees and a ninety percent chance of precipitation, bringing expected rainfall totals between a tenth and a quarter of an inch. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise will be at seven twelve a.m., and sunset at six p.m.

In Hollywood and screenwriting news, Deadline reports that the CBS daytime drama Beyond the Gates triumphed at the fifty-third annual Daytime Emmy Awards with four major wins in its first year of eligibility, including trophies for Outstanding Lead Actor and Emerging Actress. The Hollywood Reporter notes that Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff have filed for divorce after three years of marriage. Meanwhile, Variety reports that Indian filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has died at the age of fifty-nine following a fatal fall at his Mumbai residence. In publishing news, Deadline reports that Angel Studios executive Jeff Harmon has laid out a strict new values-based content standard called The Angel Promise, which bans on-screen sex, nudity, the f-word, and the misuse of God's name across its distributed projects.

In artificial intelligence and technology, The Verge reports that major AI developers including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic have agreed to back a new shared policy token standard proposed via the Internet Engineering Task Force. This new standard will allow publishers to apply website scraping preferences universally through robots.txt files instead of negotiating individually with every tech firm. TechCrunch notes that Google's first data center satellite has officially come online in space, running a Gemma four model on board its Tensor Processing Units and successfully transmitting its first AI-generated poetry back down to Earth.

Checking the weather in Rio de Janeiro, today brings light drizzle with a high near seventy-seven degrees and a low around seventy. Winds may gust up to twenty-four miles per hour, and the ultraviolet index reaches a very high level of nine. Sunrise was at five oh eight a.m., and sunset will arrive at six oh four p.m. local time.

Finally, in news from Brazil and Rio, G1 reports that local residents in Duque de Caxias experienced an intense shootout, which included a semi-truck being physically blocked across the Washington Luiz highway during ongoing security operations. Meanwhile, O Globo reports that Rio has kicked off its fourth annual Breakfast Weekend event, running through November twenty-ninth and featuring special breakfast menus at participating spots across the city.

That's the paper.
